name: platform-playbooks
description: Playbooks for answering questions about Uderia itself with TDA_Platform — inspecting an agent, explaining its trust state, a trust overview of all agents, and the user's usage this period — read one at a time.
author: Uderia
use_cases: Explaining what an agent is and what it uses
Explaining why an agent reads trusted, changed or unsigned
Summarising the trust state of all the user's agents
Summarising the user's usage and limits this period

index.title: What the deployment costs
index.summary: Where the deployment's spend goes, and where it cannot be counted: cost by model and provider, the trend, and the models running without a price.

index.title: How is the deployment doing
index.summary: The whole deployment at a glance — consumption across users, the database and backups, maintenance jobs, providers — in totals, never anyone's conversations.

index.title: Inspect an agent
index.summary: What one agent is and what it can use: its class, model, data source, components, skills and trust state, in a short answer.

index.title: Create a flow from a template
index.summary: Build a multi-step automation from one of the platform's topology templates — a pipeline, a fork–join, a debate — with the user's agents in its slots, and submit it for their approval.

index.title: Run a flow
index.summary: Run one of the user's flows now, follow the run, and report what it produced — or stop it.

index.title: Schedule a question for an agent
index.summary: Have one of the user's agents answer a question on a timer — every weekday morning, every hour — and pause, resume, change or remove such a schedule. Every schedule is approved by the user.

index.title: What runs on its own
index.summary: What the user has automated — flows and scheduled questions — and how their recent runs went.

index.title: Give an agent a knowledge graph
index.summary: Choose which knowledge graph an agent reads: assign a graph to it, make it the agent's active graph, or take it away — each submitted for the user's approval.

index.title: Change what an agent is made of
index.summary: Change an existing agent's composition — its model, its knowledge repositories, its experts, its skills, its capabilities, its context window — and submit the change for the user's approval.

index.title: Create an agent
index.summary: Compose a new agent of any class from what the user already has — its model, its data source, its knowledge, its experts, its skills and capabilities — and submit it for the user's approval.

index.title: Keep canvases tidy
index.summary: Find, rename, roll back or remove the user's canvases — the documents and code kept from conversations — each change submitted for the user's approval.

index.title: Keep dashboards in order
index.summary: Create, rename, arrange or remove the user's dashboards and their tiles, and refresh a tile through its own agent — each change submitted for the user's approval.

index.title: What the data products can answer
index.summary: Explain which data products a knowledge graph offers, what each measures and how far it is trusted, and show the SQL a request would run — without running it.

index.title: Add documents to a knowledge repository
index.summary: Put documents the user has in their Files into one of their knowledge repositories — creating the repository first when they want a new one — and submit it for their approval.

index.title: Clean up a knowledge repository
index.summary: Keep a repository's content right — quarantine or remove a wrong document, sync, screen, change settings — each submitted for the user's approval.

index.title: A graph's versions, lifecycle and conformance
index.summary: Where a knowledge graph stands — its saved versions, its lifecycle, whether it conforms, the tuning proposed for it — and saving a version before it changes.

index.title: Explore a knowledge graph
index.summary: What one of the user's knowledge graphs holds: its entity types and how they connect, the entities a question is about, and what sits next to one of them.

index.title: Check a knowledge repository's health
index.summary: How sound a knowledge repository is: what it holds, whether its documents are screened, what the screening found, what is quarantined, and which documents the user rated badly.

index.title: Try a question against a knowledge repository
index.summary: See what an agent would retrieve from a knowledge repository for a question — which documents answer it and how well — without asking the agent.

index.title: Bundle agents into a pack
index.summary: Put some of the user's agents into a new draft pack — ready to be proposed and published by the user — or keep a pack's name, description and version right.

index.title: What is in the marketplace
index.summary: Find packs others have published, read what one offers, and see what it would need from the user's data sources — without installing anything.

index.title: Is the pack ready to publish
index.summary: Whether one of the user's packs can be published now, and if not, what stands in the way and who acts next.

index.title: What needs me
index.summary: What waits for the user: incidents in the Assurance Inbox and items in the review queue — withheld answers, fired gates, changes agents submitted.

index.title: When did it get worse, and what changed
index.summary: Find when an agent's quality, cost or latency moved, and line it up with what changed around then — its model, its configuration, its signature, its knowledge.

index.title: Score a turn again, or try a policy
index.summary: Check one turn again against what a right answer says (optionally with model judges), or see what a stricter trust policy would have done to past turns — before anyone switches it on.

index.title: What is failing, and why
index.summary: Which quality checks fail, for which agents, and what the failing turns have in common — read from the scores the platform records on every turn.

index.title: What is missing to answer a question
index.summary: When no one can answer a question, find out what is missing — an expert or the data itself — and what would close the gap.

index.title: Answer a question that spans several fields
index.summary: Get a question answered that no single expert answers alone: ask the ones that fit each part and combine their answers, naming who answered what and what remains unanswered.

index.title: Get a second opinion
index.summary: Check an answer by putting the same question to another expert, and report where the two answers agree and where they differ.

index.title: Explain an agent's trust state
index.summary: Why one agent reads trusted, changed, unsigned or not attested here — named down to the ingredient that decides it.

index.title: Trust across my agents
index.summary: Which of the user's agents are trusted, changed, unsigned or not attested here — one overview.

index.title: My usage this period
index.summary: What the user has spent this period — tokens, cost, turns, limits — and where it went.
